newsitem.title: CHINA: China makers overhaul Japan in electrical goods.
newsitem.headline: China makers overhaul Japan in electrical goods.

text.p: Chinese manufacturers have overhauled Japan in sales of refrigerators, washing machines and rice cookers in the Shanghai market but lag behind in televisions and photographic equipment, a newspaper said on Thursday.

A survey of major department stores and specialist shops found that three Chinese makers account for 86.7 percent of the city's refrigerator market and three other Chinese makers 64.6 percent of the washing machine market, Wen Hui Bao reported.
Chinese firms also had 77.9 percent of the rice cooker market, it said.

But Japanese brands account for 100 percent of sales of video cameras, 85 percent of sales of video cassette machines, 36.9 percent of sales of sound systems and 43.1 percent of sales of colour televisions, it said.
It said Shanghai consumers are buying a wider range of goods than in the 1970s and 1980s.
The average spending on a colour television in 1995 was 5,576 yuan, up from 1,291 yuan in 1988, and on a refrigerator was 2,674 yuan, up from 1,532 yuan, it said.
